body.statement:
Let \(N\ge 1\), and let \(Y_1,\ldots,Y_N\) be independent real-valued random variables such that \(a_i\le Y_i\le b_i\) almost surely.  Put \(\overline Y=N^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^N Y_i\) and \(\mu=\mathbb E[\overline Y]\).  Then, for every \(u>0\),
\[
 \Pr\{\overline Y-\mu\ge u\}
 \le
 \exp\!\left\{-\frac{2N^2u^2}{\sum_{i=1}^N(b_i-a_i)^2}\right\}.
\]

source.verbatim_statement: Theorem 2. If \(X_1,\ldots,X_n\) are independent and \(a_i\le X_i\le b_i\), then for \(t>0\), \(\Pr\{\overline X-\mu\ge t\}\le \exp\{-2n^2t^2/\sum_{i=1}^n(b_i-a_i)^2\}\).

attestation.note: Transcribed from the displayed statement of Theorem 2 and equation (2.6) on page 16 of the accessible scan of the primary article.
